anchor.quote: Let $B = 2^k$ be the radix, the base in which each integer is written
with $k$ the number of bits in each radix digit
Let $d$ be the number of radix digits of each input.
Let $x$ and $y$ be the two inputs, nonnegative integers below $B^d$.
Let $x$ and $y$ be the two inputs, nonnegative integers below $B^d$.
Let $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{d-1})$ be the coefficient list of $x$, its radix digits
its radix digits, so that $x = \sum_{i=0}^{d-1} a_i B^i$ with $0 \le a_i < B$
Let $z$ be a formal variable, a placeholder for the powers of a polynomial.
The input $y$ has the coefficient list $b$ in the same way.
The convolution $c = a * b$ is the coefficient list of the product $a(z)b(z)$

gaps.note: The page presents transforming a and b, multiplying pointwise and inverting as computing the convolution when the transform length is at least 2d-1. Nothing given shows why a pointwise product of transforms yields the coefficient convolution (the convolution theorem) or why length 2d-1 suffices.
